Start small - find out what the differences are and what you like.

Me - scotch. Scotchy scotch scotch. It's distilled from malted barley and aged for a minimum of .... 4 years I think. Typically 12 is entry point, and 15, 16, and 18 is getting decent. The barley is not overpowering, so much of the flavor and nuance of the drink is derived from the region it was distilled in and the barrel it was matured in.

Bourbon is made from a corn mash and has a much sweeter taste. It isn't aged as long and uses new oak casks for the aging process.

Rye is similar to bourbons in that it is a staple of the American south, but rye is used instead of corn. It isn't as sweet.

There is also Canadian whisky, which is a good mixing whisky. Japan and Taiwan have fantastic single malts right now that have beat out scotches for the best whisky in the world several times in the last few years.

Drinking whisky:

You can drink it neat, which is room temp out of the bottle. You can add ice to cool it, but it will throw off the flavors. You can also add a few drops of distilled water to a good single malt to "open it up." A lot of the aromatics and flavored can get trapped in long hydrocarbon chains that are broken up with the introduction of the water, and the profile will change.

I'm into whisky, but there are others who are into tequila. I don't think there is as much variety and nuance there, but it still exists. Vodka shouldn't have taste. Cognac ....I know very little.
